_readme: A COMPLETE four-workflow lifecycle campaign in deploy_workflow.py spec format. Every value is a placeholder. Replace every REPLACE_ME_* string, then: python3 deploy_workflow.py --spec workflow-spec.starter.json  (validate)  then --deploy. Keys starting with _ are annotations and are stripped before deploy. Triggers are NOT deployable — the trigger field is a note for the human/browser step.
_action_types_covered: add_contact_tag, remove_contact_tag, event_start_date, email, wait (elapsed AND event-anchored), if_else (with real then/else branches), remove_from_workflow, add_to_workflow, remove_from_all_workflows, sms, add_notes, internal_notification, create_opportunity, update_contact_field, dnd_contact, goto
name: REPLACE_ME_PREFIX · 1 Registered
trigger: Form submitted — the registration form. SET THIS IN THE UI; there is no trigger API.

steps._note: This workflow is the PRODUCER of the 'registered' tag that WF4 triggers on. Every tag a condition reads needs a producer somewhere or the branch is decoration.
steps.name: Tag: registered

steps._note: THE ANCHOR. Sets the clock for every event-anchored wait below. If this custom value is blank or unparseable the anchor never resolves and BOTH reminders below silently never send. Highest-consequence empty string in the build.
steps.name: Event Start Date

steps._note: template_id + templatesource:'email-builder' is the join to a saved template. Create templates FIRST; a pointer to nothing sends nothing.
steps.name: E1 Confirmation

steps._note: EVENT-ANCHORED wait: type is 'appointment' (NOT 'time'), value is in MINUTES, and it counts BACKWARD from the anchor. appointmentCondition 'skip' means a late registrant skips this reminder instead of receiving it after the fact. startAfter is deliberately absent — anchored timing lives in appointmentStartAfter.
steps.name: 1 day before the event

steps._note: update_contact_field writes a per-CONTACT custom FIELD. Not the same thing as a per-ACCOUNT custom VALUE.
steps.name: Stamp registration source

_readme: Post-event, no-show path. Demonstrates sibling exclusion and a REAL branch.
name: REPLACE_ME_PREFIX · 2 Did not attend
trigger: Tag added — did-not-attend. NOTE: nothing in this spec produces that tag; your webinar platform or an attendance-inference workflow must.

steps._note: COLD START: workflow_id must be a REAL id, which does not exist until WF1 has been deployed once. Deploy once to mint ids (they land in --state), paste them here, deploy again. An empty or placeholder id deploys with a 200 and does nothing at all.
steps.name: Remove from WF1 Registered

steps._note: ELAPSED wait: type 'time', counts forward from the moment the contact reaches this step. Correct here because the entry tag is applied right after the session.
steps.name: wait 24 hours

steps._note: A REAL BRANCH. 'then' and 'else' compile to the three-node shape GHL actually stores: this condition-node plus a branch-yes and a branch-no node, with each path hanging off its branch node. Listing these emails AFTER the if_else instead would make both of them run for everybody. The branch is inert until something applies 'watched-replay' — e.g. a link-click trigger on the replay button.
steps.name: Watched the replay?

then._note: Copy here may assert 'you watched the replay'. Match every message to the state its branch proves.
then.name: E7 Watched, did not act

attributes.subject: Can I ask what's holding you up?

attributes.html: Watched the replay, no purchase yet.

attributes.subject: You haven't opened the replay yet

else._note: sms carries its copy inline — there is no template pointer, unlike email. Include an opt-out.
else.name: SMS nudge

attributes.body: The replay is still up: {{custom_values.replay_url}} — reply STOP to opt out.

_readme: Attended path. Removes from BOTH siblings so the three post-event states stay mutually exclusive.
name: REPLACE_ME_PREFIX · 3 Attended
trigger: Tag added — attended. Producer: your webinar platform.

steps.name: Remove from WF2 Did not attend
E5 Was there something I didn't answer?

attributes.subject: Was there something I didn't answer?

steps._note: Both pipeline ids are REQUIRED and are not discoverable from this tool — read them from the pipelines API or the builder URL. An empty one deploys and creates nothing.
steps.name: Open an opportunity

steps._note: internal_notification goes to your TEAM, not the contact.
steps.name: Tell the team

_readme: Closing path. Demonstrates purchase suppression, add_to_workflow, dnd_contact and goto.
name: REPLACE_ME_PREFIX · 4 Closing
trigger: Tag added — registered. Producer: WF1 above.

steps._note: Purchase suppresses everything. Nothing in this spec produces 'purchased' — wire it to the order form or payment trigger, or this branch never takes the 'then' path.
steps.name: Purchased?

then._note: includeCurrent false keeps THIS workflow running so the steps below still execute. Set true to stop everything including this one.
then.name: Suppress all marketing

then._note: Stop all outbound for this contact. 'enable' turns DND ON.
then.name: Do not disturb

then._note: Hand off to an onboarding workflow. Same empty-id trap as remove_from_workflow.
then.name: Add to onboarding

else._note: This step pins its own id so the goto below can target it. Any step may pin an id; ids left out are minted as uuid4 at compile time.
else.name: E9 Closing this one out

else._note: goto is the ONLY way two branches rejoin — targetNodeId must be a step id in THIS workflow. The linter checks that; the API does not. Point it at a real step before deploying; this self-reference is only here to keep the starter valid.
else.name: Jump
